lines: Phase P16 is a batch of user-directed fixes surfaced after P15 shipped, grouped into one phase rather than reopening P1/P9/P10/P11/P14; it is not a planned deliverable.
P16 adds an explicit per-connection preconnect-mode checkbox that overrides P11's settle-window auto-detection.
P16 adds a connection-kind icon picker and a click-to-open connection-error popover.
P16 gives scripts/demo-dbs/ full six-engine coverage.
P16 adds testcontainers preset packages for Postgres, MariaDB and Redis, and fixes two font-family bugs.

The adapter min/max version compatibility suite runs each database/queue adapter's existing conformance tests against the oldest and newest server image its Go client library supports for that kind; those versions are set by what the client library actually supports.
The adapter compatibility suite is on-demand and does not run as part of the regular CI/test run.
The connection-add UI shows a note per connection kind stating its minimum supported server version.
Developing against one pinned test-fixture server version never catches version-boundary bugs, which is why the compatibility suite tests version extremes.
v1.3 G5 covers refs/tags/branches, checkout with the Go pre-flight engine, revert, linked-worktree detection, an in-progress banner, and an undo slot.
P15 part 1 is the presentation half of the request builder UX pass, covering eight of twelve user-reported items; the editor-behaviour half is P15b.
The response panel, including its chrome and pane switcher, is present from the moment a request tab opens rather than appearing only after a first send.
A status code's meaning is shown on its own always-visible line, replacing a truncatable caption plus a hover.
The Studio/Api mode-switch buttons are sized to the app's own tab metrics and now render the icon that modes.ts has declared unused since P1.

The .p-input class is inline-flex, so a TextField is about 20 characters wide wherever placed unless its call site says otherwise; this is the root cause of both the narrow headers/params/form-data table fields and the URL field never growing.

A new shared Checkbox primitive matching the app's design system replaces all fourteen raw input type=checkbox call sites app-wide, Studio included, because primitives already live in the shared theme layer (AppButton, TextField and SegmentedControl are precedent).
JSON is promoted to its own top-level body mode as a UI-level promotion over unchanged code+codeLanguage storage, not a new wire/Go/Postman vocabulary or a data migration.
A request's tab shows a body-present indicator via a new optional badge() member on the tab-kind registry, which answers what P4 D15 declined.
The toolbar is reflowed so Save sits with the request's name in the view head and the URL field takes the row.
P15 part 1 is sequenced after P12/P13 so it refines a surface already settled into its final module shape and design-system pass, rather than files about to be renamed or restyled.

P15 was split into part 1 and P15b because the halves fail differently, P15b opens with a packages/api-core foundation commit unrelated to these eight fixes, and part 1 touches Studio (nine checkbox call sites and the title bar) so one review pass carries that risk.
The plan for P15 is in plans/P15-request-builder-ux.md.

v1.7 M1 adds a new Go MCP server for local databases, sibling to internal/repomap, reusing its transport pattern (go-sdk/mcp, loopback-only streamable HTTP) but with its own process, port and tool set.
The DB MCP server exposes list_connections (every configured connection the app knows), list_databases, list_schemas, describe_table and run_query.
The DB MCP server's metadata tools (list_databases, list_schemas, describe_table) route through the existing apps/kira-studio/internal/adapters/* layer, with no new metadata path.
run_query executes through the same adapter query path the console UI uses.

MCP auth is a static bearer token with 7-day expiry and rotation, built directly into internal/mcpauth (not a sibling package), so the DB server's token and the repo-map server's token share one mechanism.
By explicit instruction, the repo-map server's currently non-expiring token gains the identical 7-day rotation, not a second scheme.

The M1 plan must design the expiry/rotation record shape, the rotation trigger (auto-remint on expiry vs. manual remint, possibly differing per server given the repo-map server's headless usage), and the DB server's start/stop lifecycle and storage root (shared KIRA_HOME or distinct).
Return a distinct, actionable error to a client whose token has lapsed, not a generic 401.
The DB MCP server is the first phase of the chapter: later phases (permissions, EXPLAIN, Faker, anonymization) extend its tool set or query path, so nothing else can start before it exists.

The Api module has seven request settings, global in Settings and overridable per request: httpVersion, requestTimeoutMs, maxResponseMb, sslVerify, followRedirects, maxRedirects, disableCookieJar. Defaults: HTTP version 2, timeout 0 (none), max response 50 MB, SSL verify on, follow redirects on, max redirects 10, disable cookie jar on.
Go's httpclient.Send takes an Options struct (all pointer fields, nil means default) instead of reading package constants.
resolveSendOptions/orGlobal in bridge/http.go resolve a request's seven null-means-inherit tab-state leaves against the global settings before every send.
Setting sslVerify to false shows a plain-prose security warning taken verbatim from the plan, per CLAUDE.md's carve-out for that class of text.
Cookies use one process-wide cookiejar.Jar keyed by publicsuffix; incognito sends use a throwaway per-send jar.
Response has SentCookies and ReceivedCookies, taken from the trace's WroteHeaderField hook and every hop's own Set-Cookie.

A single CookiesPane.vue component serves two modes: request mode shows what the jar would send next (debounced on URL change and after every send); response mode shows sent/received cookies grouped by hop.
The new cookie fields are masked for secrets like every other response field, via two new loops in maskSecrets.
Grow-field textarea fix 1: the textarea's UA padding of 2px was absent from the sizing replica; fixed by matching it.

Grow-field textarea fix 2: a grid item's normal alignment resolves to start, not stretch, for a replaced box with an intrinsic size (textarea via rows), so the textarea stayed 1 row tall and scrolled; fixed with align-self: stretch.

The overlay never painted on a grow textarea because the selector .input-wrap input.has-overlay didn't match a textarea; it was widened to input.has-overlay, textarea.has-overlay, with line-height: inherit so overlay lines don't drift.
The dev container has no display, so GUI launches are not possible; the Playwright ui project is the repo's established substitute for GUI-driven checks.

P98 is prep only: it adds shadcn-vue, Tailwind CSS, VueUse, Pinia and TanStack Query as standing dependencies with minimal bootstrap wiring, and migrates no existing .vue file, component, store or styling.
P98 lands the dependency and convention baseline before migration so P99 migrates onto libraries already wired and configured, not setup and migration in one pass.

Each future phase's planning pass must adapt its design to lean on the P98-wired libraries (e.g. new UI styling goes through Tailwind, not custom CSS) rather than hand-rolling equivalents, even where the spec doesn't say so. Codified in CLAUDE.md.
Every Vue component must use <script setup lang="ts"> (Composition API only, no Options API). Codified in CLAUDE.md.
Pinia stores follow single-responsibility: one store, one concern, never a grab-bag app-wide store.
Root package.json gained pinia 4.0.3, @tanstack/vue-query 5.103.2 and @vueuse/core 15.0.0, following the monaco-editor/slickgrid precedent; VueUse needs no bootstrap step.
bun install prints a peer-dependency warning for @vue/devtools-api@6.6.4 (pinia's optional devtools peer), which the app's bootstrap does not use; it is recorded, not silenced.

state/pinia.ts exports the single createPinia() instance, and state/queryClient.ts exports a single QueryClient with retry: false and refetchOnWindowFocus: false, because every query goes over the Wails bridge to the local Go process, not the network.
main.ts registers the Pinia and TanStack Query plugins as separate statements before directive/mount, replacing the earlier single chained createApp(App).directive(...).mount('#app').

The @ alias maps to ./src in both vite.config.ts resolve.alias and tsconfig.json compilerOptions.paths; existing source keeps relative imports, and @/ is used for shadcn-vue's generated import specifiers.
The shadcn-vue config uses the reka-ui base, nova style, neutral base color, lucide icons and CSS variables; it is in components.json, src/lib/utils.ts and src/theme/shadcn-bridge.css.

src/theme/shadcn-bridge.css maps every shadcn-vue variable to an existing --kira-* token, with no .dark block, because tokens.css is a single :root and index.html hardcodes class="dark". base.css imports it after ./vscode-bridge.css.
The shadcn-vue icon dependency is @lucide/vue 1.47.0, not lucide-vue-next, because the CLI's registry response for the lucide icon library names it.

knip.json has ignoreDependencies entries for @vueuse/core, reka-ui, class-variance-authority, tw-animate-css, @lucide/vue, clsx and tailwind-merge, plus a workspace ignore for src/lib/utils.ts, so unused-dependency checks stay clean.
src/lib/utils.ts combines clsx imports into one import statement and gives cn() an explicit : string return type, following the repo's single-import style.
shadcn-vue 2.8.2 does not support the --dry-run, --diff and --view options.
Never unset HTTPS_PROXY to work around a proxy-related tool failure, because docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md says that is never the fix.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Stack table has a row for the frontend library baseline (Vue/Vite/Tailwind v4/shadcn-vue-on-Reka/Pinia/TanStack Query/VueUse). P99 will migrate the app's existing 39 reactive() modules and 200 .vue files onto these libraries.

Studio stores the whole connection URI encrypted (opaque) under cipher scope connection-uri, replacing the earlier refused-keys handling for sslpassword, tlsCertificateKeyFilePassword and proxyPassword.
Whole-URI encryption was chosen because the refused URI keys sslpassword, tlsCertificateKeyFilePassword and proxyPassword still landed as plaintext in stored URIs on some paths.
SecretsRepo.GetURI is the only reader of the stored connection URI.
Connection summaries carry uri: null; no screen derives display from the URI (the connection name shows).
The connection URI is shown fully masked by default; Show and Copy URI go through the gated reveal, which decrypts it for viewing and editing, and Save re-encrypts it.
Already-stored URIs were not migrated, because nobody else uses the app; the stripping code and startup migration were removed, and old plaintext rows fail loudly.
The plan for Studio URI encryption is in plans/P181-studio-uri-encryption.md.

DropdownMenuContent in git-ui (RowContextMenu.vue) needs prioritize-position, because reka's Popper runs shift before flip by default and a 0×0 point anchor lets shift alone clamp overflow to zero, starving flip of a signal.
The git-ui force-delete confirmation is a reka Popover that dismisses on outside-click or Escape; the old hand-rolled popup never did.
In App.vue, onClickOutside takes ignore ['[data-reka-popper-content-wrapper]'] so the force-delete Popover's outside-click does not trigger the detail-region's dismiss handler.
git-ui owns its helpers cn, rowVariants and menuModel in packages/git-ui lib/{cn,rowVariants,menuModel}.ts instead of importing them from kira-ui; menuModel.test.ts moved there too.

badgeVariants is defined only in badgeClass.ts, a .vue-free module so refBadges.ts can be tested with bun test; ref badges are built on badgeVariants, and REF_BADGE_CLASS and refBadgeClass live in refBadges.ts.

AttributeTooltip and TooltipAnchorBridge were hoisted from workbench into packages/theme/src/components/; AttributeTooltip.vue and state/tooltip.ts left packages/workbench with no references remaining; Studio's SlickGridHost.vue imports the hoisted component.
AttributeTooltip reads the data-kira-tip attribute (renamed from data-kui-tip); no data-kui-tip remains in the git-ui scope.
AttributeTooltip opens on keyboard focus as well as hover.
Grid tooltips in git-ui go through the hoisted AttributeTooltip, used by CommitGrid.vue, CommitMeta.vue, FileTree.vue and BranchPicker.vue.
git-ui's mount() wraps both roots in a TooltipProvider, via MountRoot.vue.
packages/git-ui/src/theme/app-shell.css no longer exists; its raw-checkbox rule became unused and the file was deleted in the MountRoot.vue conversion.
P131 Part 2 acceptance: files in scope import nothing from kira-ui except KuiColumnResizeHandle, and test:ui:space, test:webview, test:unit and test:ui:studio must pass.
packages/git-ui imports only KuiColumnResizeHandle from @kira/kira-ui, in App.vue and CommitGrid.vue.
The P131 Part 2 plan is at docs/v2.0/plans/P131-part2-git-graph.md.
packages/git-ui main.ts still imports vKuiTooltip, registers the kui-tooltip directive and imports kui-bridge.css, because Review still uses the directive until Part 3 moves it off kira-ui.
git-ui adds no wrapper layer over shadcn components: no defineComponent in the scope and no Git*Button-style wrapper files.
TagList.vue and StashRows.vue rows are raw button elements with tips as attributes, so they do not import shadcn components.
The RowContextMenu contextmenu listener lives on RowActionsButton, not on the row's checkout button.
Search Escape works in two stages: the first Escape dismisses the dropdown and keeps the query, the second clears the query and closes.
apps/kira-studio/frontend does not depend on @kira/git-ui; the only Studio file touched by P131 Part 2 is SlickGridHost.vue, with an import-path rename and a comment update.
fakeGraphHost.ts does not vary --vscode-* tokens between the body.vscode-dark and body.vscode-light classes, so host-token checks read identically in both themes.
fakeGraphHost.ts's fixture never sets capabilities.write in its app.init response, so write-gated UI (inline rename, worktree-remove dialog in App.vue/BranchPicker.vue) is unreachable from it.

fakeGraphHost.ts never mocks commit.detail (only fakeReviewHost.ts does, for the /review route), so DetailState.detail never resolves on /graph and CommitMeta/FileTree detail content never mounts there.
commit-meta-clamp.spec.ts uses its own dedicated commitMetaHarnessServer.ts mount because fakeGraphHost.ts does not mock commit.detail.
In Kira Space's test app, installGitStreamMock's extraResults can mock commit.detail, unlike fakeGraphHost.ts.

The two hosts' token tables are intentionally distinct: the search toggle Button color is rgb(157, 157, 157) under Kira Space's unprefixed --kira-* root versus rgb(204, 204, 204) under the webview's --kv-*-bridged tokens.

graphStreamFixture.ts's minimal refs.list fixture renders zero .kv-badge, so App.vue's branch-tip-to-badge overlay needs more than that fixture wires; badge rendering is covered by graph-columns.spec.ts's "ref/tag badges render as outlines" test.

A standalone Playwright config outside the apps' test trees cannot resolve @playwright/test's module graph, so scratch specs must be placed temporarily inside the real test tree (apps/kira-space-vscode/tests/interaction/ or apps/kira-space/tests/ui/).
Kira Space serves a read-only mobile-laid-out Vue agents web app (P212) from a local web server, with first-load device approval in Kira Space like the git extension pairing.
The mobile agents web app is limited to three tabs: Backlog, Need You, Plan; the user narrowed the scope.
The mobileweb server allowlist is GET only plus POST /api/pair; there is no terminal/PTY attach.
Mobile web auth uses a per-device cookie token, csrfGuard and a route table, so adding a write endpoint takes one route-table row.

P212 added generic internal/pairing and internal/embedded packages, appevent.Tap, the mobileweb server, migration 0021, a desktop Mobile access pane and pairing dialog, a transport-agnostic ADE reader, a second Vite build, and Playwright mobile projects.
The installable PWA and the local CA of the mobile web were removed in P223.
Design facts for the mobile agents web are documented in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md under "Mobile agents web (P212, Kira Space)".
The mobile web UI is verified with test:ui:space-mobile (iOS WebKit and Pixel Chromium emulation); a real phone was not verified.
The four Settings dialog snapshots in test:visual:space differ because the nav gained a "Mobile access" row; baselines must be regenerated on the reference machine.

Follow-up amendment P212 Part 2 covers backlog add and reorder, TUI input for stuck agents, start/next/prev workflow stage, and phone attach of the Claude Code terminal (desktop shows disconnected plus a reconnect button).

The Api module has seven request settings, each configurable globally in Settings and per request (overriding the global): httpVersion, requestTimeoutMs, maxResponseMb, sslVerify, followRedirects, maxRedirects, disableCookieJar.
Api setting defaults: HTTP version 2, request timeout 0 (none), max response size 50 MB, SSL verification on, auto-follow redirects on, max redirects 10, disable cookie jar on.
Go's httpclient.Send takes an Options struct (all-pointer, nil means default) instead of reading package constants.
resolveSendOptions/orGlobal in bridge/http.go resolve a request's seven null-means-inherit tab-state leaves against the global settings row before every send.
Setting sslVerify to false shows a plain-prose security warning verbatim from the plan, per CLAUDE.md's carve-out for that class of text.
Cookies use one process-wide cookiejar.Jar keyed by publicsuffix, and incognito sends use a throwaway per-send jar.
Response has SentCookies and ReceivedCookies fields, populated from the trace's WroteHeaderField hook and every hop's own Set-Cookie.

The Cookies tab reuses one CookiesPane.vue component: request mode shows what the jar would send next (debounced on URL change and after every send); response mode shows sent/received cookies grouped by hop.
Cookie secrets in the SentCookies/ReceivedCookies fields are masked by maskSecrets like other response fields (two new loops).
The grow-field multi-line bug had a first cause: the UA padding of 2px on the textarea was absent from the sizing replica; this was fixed.

A grid item's normal alignment resolves to start, not stretch, for a replaced box with an intrinsic size (CSS Box Alignment §8.3), and a textarea counts via its rows attribute, so the grow textarea stayed 1 row tall and scrolled; fixed with explicit align-self: stretch.

The overlay never painted on a grow textarea because the selector .input-wrap input.has-overlay didn't match a textarea; it was widened to input.has-overlay, textarea.has-overlay, with line-height: inherit so overlay lines don't drift past line 2.
Playwright ui-project tests are this repo's substitute for a GUI-driven check, since the dev container has no display (docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md).
Full bun run test:ui has pre-existing failures from a Monaco-editor-loading timeout (data-kira-editor-text never appears) across files such as console, grpc, cell-editor, slick-grid and sql-schema.
P90 added Go tests against a real httptest.Server covering redirects off, max-redirects, body-cap both directions, zero-timeout, cookie-jar replay including ephemeral case, and forced HTTP/1.1.

In a shared checkout, commit with an explicit pathspec (git commit -m ... -- <files>) and never git add -A or git add ., because concurrent sessions' changes would be swept in; preserve a concurrent unstaged edit with a scoped git stash push -u -- <path>, never a bare git stash.
